extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, and patent agents filing or prosecuting Canadian patent applications before CIPO
extracted.subtask_description: Official CIPO guidance on procedural requirements for Canadian patent applications, including priority restoration, priority claims, maintenance fees, public inspection, withdrawal, special character handling, abandonment, reinstatement, and the due care standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of the right of priority – effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration of the right of priority is available for patent applications that have a filing date that is on or after October 30, 2019, the coming-into-force date of the Patent Rules (SOR/2019-251).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to restore the right of priority – required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: To request restoration of priority under paragraph 28.4(6)(b) of the Patent Act and subsections 77(1) and 77(2) of the Patent Rules, the applicant must, within the relevant prescribed time: make a request for subsection 28.4(6) to apply; state that the failure to file within 12 months was unintentional; make a request for priority in the petition or in a document other than the abstract, specification or drawings; and submit the filing date and the name of the country or office of filing of the previously regularly filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be made within the prescribed time set out in section 77 of the Patent Rules (see Section 7.03.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods for request to restore right of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limits to request restoration under subsection 77(1) of the Patent Rules differ by application type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a regular (non-PCT) application – not later than two months after the filing date of the application or co-pending application; for a PCT national phase application – not later than one month after the national phase entry date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for right of priority to be deemed restored
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration of the right of priority will be recognized in Canada on the national phase entry date of a PCT national phase application or divisional resulting from the division of a PCT national phase application if: the filing date of the pending application is more than 12 months after the filing date of the previously regularly filed application, but within two months after the end of those 12 months; and if the right of priority, in respect of the previously regularly filed application, was restored under Rule 26bis.3 of the PCT Regulations and that restoration is, under Rule 49ter.1, effective in Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed restoration of right of priority – effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: The deemed restoration in Canada will be effective for PCT national phase applications with an international filing date that is on or after October 30, 2019.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for priority considered withdrawn – failure to provide priority document copy/access
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for priority will be considered withdrawn if the applicant does not comply with the requirement to provide a copy of the priority document or provide access not later than two months after the date of the notice under subsection 74(4) of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 7.04.05 for notice and timing details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for priority considered withdrawn – failure to submit priority document after compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for priority will be considered withdrawn if the applicant is considered to have complied with the requirement to provide a copy or access but does not submit a copy of the priority document not later than three months after the day on which it is required by subsection 74(8) of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 7.04.06 for further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for priority considered withdrawn – failure to provide translation
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for priority will be considered withdrawn if the applicant does not provide a translation of the priority document, a new translation, or a statement by the translator and a new translation within four months of the date of the relevant notice sent under subsection 76(1) or 76(2) of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 7.05 for translation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of a request for priority – procedure and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may withdraw a request for priority by request to the Commissioner. The effective date of withdrawal is the date the Commissioner receives the request. Withdrawal may affect the claim date and applicable prior art (sections 28.1–28.3 of the Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawing a priority request may delay or change the confidentiality/public inspection timing (see Chapter 8). Withdrawal before the expiry of the confidentiality period may allow delaying laying open to public inspection until eighteen months from the next earliest priority date or the filing date if no other priority documents exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claims from applications before intergovernmental organisations
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request priority in Canada based on a previously filed application submitted to an intergovernmental organisation (e.g., ARIPO); the applicant should identify the organisation as the authority and provide the filing date and application number issued by that organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: identify ARIPO as the authority and provide the ARIPO application number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claims from applications filed before international organisations
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications filed before an international organisation (that examines but does not grant a national patent) may form the basis of priority for applications filed in Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claims from PCT applications – effect of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a PCT application has the effect of filing a regular national application in each designated state; the Canadian filing date of the national phase application equals the PCT filing date and priority rights may be based on an international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming priority from an internationally filed application, identify the receiving office (e.g., 'IB' for the International Bureau) and provide the assigned application number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claims from EPO applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Office acknowledges priority based on an application filed with the European Patent Office (EPO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time not permissible for priority recognition information
rubrics_metrics.description: Although subsection 3(1) generally permits extensions of time, subsection 73(7) of the Patent Rules provides that the Commissioner is not permitted to extend time limits for providing the Office information necessary to recognise a request for priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolling for prescribed and designated days for twelve‑month priority period
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the twelve-month anniversary date is a prescribed or designated day (e.g., a day when the Patent Office is closed), filing of the pending application may be made on the next day that is not a prescribed or designated day without forfeiting priority rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to the twelve-month anniversary date defined in paragraph 28.1(1)(b) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of ownership – evidence to establish priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant named on the priority document differs from the Canadian applicant, the applicant in Canada is recommended to furnish the Patent Office with evidence that priority rights have been transferred to satisfy subparagraph 28.1(1)(a)(i) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of recognised priority documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Office recognizes Paris Convention priority based on petty patent applications, applications for inventors’ certificates, and utility models filed in foreign countries as forms of patent applications. No priority rights may be based on industrial design registrations, design patents or their equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees for patent applications – requirement and start date
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who files a patent application in Canada must pay annual maintenance fees starting at the 2nd anniversary of the filing date to maintain the application in effect (subsection 27.1(1) of the Patent Act and section 68 of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 5 for who can pay and for late fees information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amounts and due dates for maintenance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The amounts and time limits for paying maintenance fees are listed on CIPO’s Patent Fees webpage. Maintenance fees are due annually on or before the anniversary of the filing date, starting on the 2nd anniversary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees may be paid in advance; time limits for payment of maintenance fees for applications cannot be extended (subsection 68(3) of the Patent Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Late fee period for maintenance fees – notice and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: If the required maintenance fee is not paid on or before the anniversary date, a prescribed late fee is also required. A Commissioner’s Notice will be sent shortly after the due date and the notice will require payment of the maintenance fee and late fee before the later of: six months after the maintenance fee due date; or two months after the date of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fees are not paid within the late fee period, the application will be deemed abandoned under paragraph 73(1)(c). Payments during the late fee period will be acknowledged to the default correspondent in a courtesy letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees for divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisional applications carry their own maintenance fees, separate from the parent application. Maintenance fees are calculated as a function of the filing date of the divisional (which is the same as the parent application). All maintenance fees between the filing date and the presentation date of the divisional are due on the presentation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not paid by that date, a Commissioner’s Notice will require payment of fees and a single late fee before the later of six months after the presentation date or two months after the date of the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees for PCT national phase entry applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications entering the Canadian national phase under the PCT must pay maintenance fees at the date of PCT national phase entry. The international filing date is the date on which the maintenance fee schedule is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See CIPO’s Patent Fees webpage for amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection – timing and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: All patent applications are opened to public inspection after the end of an eighteen-month confidentiality period under section 10 of the Patent Act. The fundamental purpose is to encourage innovation by disclosing invention details to the public as the trade-off for time-limited monopoly rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The end of the confidentiality period is the earlier of: eighteen months from the Canadian filing date, or (if a priority request was made) eighteen months from the earliest filing date of any previously regularly filed application on which the request for priority is based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection of PCT national phase applications
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT applications are laid open to public inspection by WIPO eighteen months after filing or from the earliest priority date; if the application was published in English or French by WIPO on or before Canadian national phase entry, it is considered open to public inspection in Canada as of the international publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If WIPO publication did not occur on or before national phase entry, the public inspection date will be when it is laid open to the public in Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early public inspection (Early Laid Open)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may make a written request to have an application opened to public inspection before the expiry of the confidentiality period (commonly known as 'Early Laid Open').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no fee for this service request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and controlled access to unopened applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications not yet open to public inspection are confidential under section 10 and sections 16–18 of the Patent Rules. The Commissioner will provide access only to the applicant, the appointed patent agent, or any person authorized by the applicant or common representative. Authorized persons must provide identification and a signed authorization document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventors who have assigned all interest cannot access an unopened file without authorization. If an agent is appointed and an inventor retains some interest, interviews discussing prosecution in detail are permitted only in the agent’s presence or with the agent’s consent (section 39).

rubrics_metrics.name: Means to access applications open to public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: After an application is laid open to public inspection, the application, complete prosecution history and all documents may be viewed in person at CIPO, purchased online via the Data and Document Dissemination Section, or obtained by contacting that section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact details for the Data and Document Dissemination Section are provided for obtaining files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canadian Patents Database availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Canadian Patent Database (CPD) is an online database available 24/7 where applications, patents, administrative information and most filed documents are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the CPD for more information; link provided in original guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting personal information on the Canadian Patents Database
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Office will endeavour to prevent posting of sensitive personal information to the CPD if documents are expressly identified by the applicant as having sensitive personal content. Applicants are recommended to provide sensitive personal information in a separate supporting document clearly marked as sensitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further information is provided via a linked guidance page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of lists of granted patents and newly opened applications
rubrics_metrics.description: On Tuesdays (except statutory holidays) the Office publishes a list of all patents granted during the week ending that Tuesday and a list of all patent applications that became open to public inspection during that week on the CIPO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of patent applications – procedure and possible refund
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be withdrawn at any time by a written request from the person authorized to represent the applicant. It may be possible to refund certain fees if the application was filed through inadvertence, accident or mistake and withdrawn not later than the fourteenth day after the earliest date that the documents were submitted to establish a filing date or entry into national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refund rules differ for regular Canadian applications and international (PCT) applications (see paragraph 139(1)(b) and (c) of the Patent Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of withdrawal on applications being open to public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Under subsection 10(5) of the Patent Act, an application will be removed from active files and not be made open to public inspection if withdrawn on or before the earlier of: the day that is two months before the end of the confidentiality period and, if applicable, the day on which an early opening request is made. Withdrawal after the end of confidentiality and before issue will remove the application from active files but will not undo publication already in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of withdrawal of priority on opening to public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for priority may be withdrawn at any time before a patent is issued. If withdrawn at an early stage, it may be possible to delay the opening of the application to public inspection; the withdrawal must be made within sixteen months of the filing date of the earliest priority application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section 17 of the Patent Rules; the application will be laid open at the end of the new confidentiality period (eighteen months from the Canadian filing or from earliest priority date if multiple).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover page publication and corrections – content and immutability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Office prepares a cover page when the application is laid open and again upon grant. The cover page contains specified bibliographic fields (e.g., filing date, issue date, priority data, title, applicant/inventor names, IPC, abstract/claims converted to searchable text). The cover page is a static document and cannot be altered under normal circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent bibliographic changes will not re-create the cover page but will be visible in Office records and the CPD; database corrections may produce overnight updates to online records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special characters – conversion practice and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to technical limitations, some special characters (letters with accents, most Greek characters, etc.) cannot be entered or reliably reproduced in Office records. Special characters transcribed into the database will be entered according to a Special Character Conversion Table and will appear converted in bibliographic information and correspondence. Characters in documents stored only as images are not affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover Page characters are not affected by this limitation, so special characters may appear on the Cover Page but not on other database-produced documents. A conversion table (Latin and Greek) specifies exact replacements (e.g., é -> E, ñ -> N, α -> .ALPHA.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed abandonment under subsection 73(1) – causes
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall be deemed abandoned under subsection 73(1) if: the applicant does not reply in good faith to any requisition made by an examiner within four months of the requisition date; does not comply with a compliance notice under subsection 27(6) within three months; fails to pay maintenance fee and late fee before the later of six months after due date and two months after notice; fails to make required request for examination and pay fee and late fee before two months after notice; or fails to make the request for examination and pay fee before three months after notice in the case referred to in subsection 35(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple, concurrent or overlapping abandonments are possible; responsibility to meet obligations lies with the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed abandonment under subsection 73(2) (subsection 132(1) of Patent Rules) – causes
rubrics_metrics.description: An application will be deemed abandoned under subsection 73(2) in any circumstance provided for in subsection 132(1) of the Patent Rules, including: failure to comply with notice under subsection 15(4) to provide a translation within two months; failure to comply with appointment-of-agent notice under section 31 within three months; failure to respond in good faith to request for further drawings under 27(5.2) within three months; failure to respond in good faith to a notice under section 65 requiring modification within specified time; failure to request continued examination and pay prescribed fee under subsection 85.1(3); failure to pay final fee after notice of allowance under applicable subsections; failure to reply in good faith to conditional notice of allowance and pay final fee; failure to comply with notice under subsection 155.5(6) within the referred time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courtesy letters of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: While not required by the Patent Act or Patent Rules, the Patent Office will endeavour to inform applicants of deemed abandonments through a courtesy letter. Applicants will have received prior notice of the potential for abandonment if they failed to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of abandoned patent applications – general requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is deemed abandoned under subsection 73(1) or 73(2), it may be reinstated under subsection 73(3) within 12 months of the date deemed abandoned by: making a request for reinstatement to the Commissioner; taking the action that should have been taken to avoid abandonment; and paying the reinstatement fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 12-month period and reinstatement fee are prescribed by sections 133 and 134 of the Patent Rules; see Chapter 9 for more specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement fee – single request for related failures
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is abandoned because the applicant failed to respond to an examiner’s requisition and failed to request continued examination, the applicant does not need to pay two fees to request reinstatement as long as both failures are mentioned in the reinstatement request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies when both failures are due to the same underlying circumstances and included in one request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatements requiring a positive determination of due care
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain reinstatements require a positive determination by the Commissioner that the failure occurred 'in spite of the due care required by the circumstances having been taken' under paragraph 73(3)(b). Specifically: failure to pay the maintenance fee (73(1)(c)); and failure to request examination/pay the fee when more than six months has elapsed after the prescribed date to request examination under 35(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests requiring a due care determination should be accompanied by a statement of the reasons for the failure which led to abandonment; see Section 9.04 for application of the due care standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for reinstatement – 12 months and illustrative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Once deemed abandoned, the applicant has 12 months to reinstate. Examples illustrate how abandonment dates and the 12‑month reinstatement deadline are calculated for requisitions, maintenance fee non-payment, and Commissioner’s notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show how calendar and notice timing affect the deemed abandonment date and the corresponding reinstatement deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single request for reinstatement for multiple abandonments – conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A single request to reinstate may be made for multiple failures so long as a reinstatement fee is paid in respect of each failure and all actions are taken to rectify all failures that caused the abandonments. The reinstatement requests must be made before the end of the first reinstatement period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due care standard – scope and application
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments implementing the Patent Law Treaty introduce a due care standard that must be met before an application deemed abandoned can be reinstated after: failure to pay a maintenance fee and late fee; failure to request examination or (if applicable) pay the examination fee, when the request for reinstatement is received after 6 months from the prescribed date to request examination. The Commissioner must make a positive determination that due care was taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 9.04 for details on evidence and reasoning required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional provisions for due care
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant requesting reinstatement following failure to pay a maintenance fee or failure to request examination that occurred prior to October 30, 2019 is not subject to the due care standard; the previous section 73 as it read immediately before October 30, 2019 applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of due care by the Commissioner – applicant obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: To enable the Commissioner to determine due care, the applicant is required to provide the reasons for the failure to take the action that should have been taken to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should submit a statement of reasons and supporting evidence when a due care determination is required.
